videos.script: Lesson 11 found out who is asking. Today, what they may do. {{title}} You start by finding a hole. Carla has an account and organises nothing. She changes two events, and the API says 200. {{hole}} Then two status codes that are easy to mix up. 401 means: I do not know who you are. 403 means: I know who you are, and no. {{codes}} A permission says what kind of thing someone may do. Bruno may change events. It says nothing about which ones. So events get an organiser. {{owner}} In DRF, two classes must agree. One for the kind of request, one for the row. Bruno changes his own event, and not Ana's. {{drf}} FastAPI has no permission system. A guard is a dependency that raises 403. You write two: one for a role, one for ownership. {{guards}} And the same small script runs against both APIs, as four people, through four doors. The two tables agree, cell by cell. Except one, and you see why.
